questions.question: Neither the Chola nor the Chera dynasty was directly responsible for the establishment of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahmani kingdom**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Bahmani kingdom** was established in **1347 CE** by **Ala-ud-din Bahman Shah** after revolting against the Delhi Sultanate's Tughlaq dynasty. It was the first independent Islamic kingdom in southern India. 
• Neither the **Chola dynasty** nor the **Chera dynasty** played any role in the establishment of the Bahmani kingdom, as their reigns predated the formation of this kingdom by several centuries. 
• The Bahmani kingdom was located in the **Deccan region** and was known for its distinct Indo-Islamic culture, architecture, and administrative systems. 
• The establishment of the Bahmani kingdom marked the beginning of an era of Islamic dominance in the Deccan region, which later saw the rise of other prominent kingdoms like the **Bijapur Sultanate** and the **Golconda Sultanate**. 
• The Chola and Chera dynasties were primarily associated with the Tamil region and were recognized for their contributions to **Tamil literature, naval expeditions, and temple architecture**, which were distinct from the Bahmani kingdom's focus on Islamic culture and governance. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Chola dynasty:** 
• The Chola dynasty was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in Indian history, spanning from the late 9th century to the 13th century CE. 
• They are renowned for their contributions to **Tamil literature**, the construction of grand temples like the **Brihadeeswarar Temple** in Thanjavur, and their extensive **naval expeditions** to Southeast Asia. 
• The Cholas played a significant role in the promotion of Hindu culture and the establishment of a sophisticated administrative system. 
• **Chera dynasty:** 
• The Chera dynasty was one of the ancient Tamil dynasties that ruled parts of present-day Kerala and Tamil Nadu. 
• Their contributions included fostering **Tamil literary renaissance** and trade relations with the Romans, Greeks, and Arabs. 
• They were known for their involvement in the **spice trade** and the development of maritime commerce. 
• **Bahmani kingdom:** 
• The Bahmani kingdom lasted for nearly two centuries, from **1347 CE to 1527 CE**, before breaking into five successor states known as the **Deccan Sultanates**. 
• The kingdom's capital was initially **Gulbarga** and later moved to **Bidar**. 
• The Bahmani rulers were known for their patronage of Persian culture, art, and architecture, including the construction of notable monuments like the **Gol Gumbaz**. 
• **Devadasi temple system:** 
• The **Devadasi system** was prominent during the Chola and Chera reigns, where women dedicated themselves to temple services, including dance and music. 
• It was deeply rooted in Hindu culture and had no connection to the Islamic Bahmani kingdom. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Geographical distinction:** The Chola and Chera dynasties were centered in the Tamil region, whereas the Bahmani kingdom was established in the Deccan region of southern India. 
• **Chronological difference:** The Chola and Chera dynasties flourished several centuries before the Bahmani kingdom emerged. 
• **Religious and cultural contrast:** The Cholas and Cheras were deeply rooted in Hindu traditions, whereas the Bahmani kingdom represented Islamic governance and culture. 
• **Architectural legacy:** The Cholas and Cheras are celebrated for their temple architecture, while the Bahmani kingdom is known for its Indo-Islamic architectural styles. </ul

questions.question: Which of these countries is known as the "Land of the Thunder Dragon"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhutan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhutan** is famously known as the **"Land of the Thunder Dragon"** due to its association with the mythical dragon, "Druk," which appears on its national flag and symbolizes thunder.
 
• The term "Thunder Dragon" originates from the local name for Bhutan, **"Druk Yul,"** which translates to "Land of the Thunder Dragon."
 
• The national flag of Bhutan features a dragon, which represents the country's identity and connection to its mythology. The dragon holds jewels, symbolizing protection and wealth.
 
• Bhutan is a small, landlocked country situated in the eastern Himalayas, bordered by **India** to the south and **China** to the north.
 
• Bhutan's culture is deeply rooted in **Buddhist traditions**, and the dragon plays a significant role in its religious beliefs and folklore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Location:**

 
 
• Bhutan is located in the eastern Himalayas and is known for its mountainous terrain, forests, and diverse ecosystems.
 
• The capital city of Bhutan is **Thimphu**, which serves as the political and cultural hub of the country.
 
 
 
• **Cultural and Religious Influence:**
 
 
• Bhutan is predominantly Buddhist, and its cultural heritage revolves around Buddhist practices, monasteries, and festivals.
 
• The dragon symbol, "Druk," is deeply intertwined with Bhutan's **Dzongkha language** and religious texts.
 
 
 
• **Economy:**
 
 
• Bhutan's economy is largely dependent on **agriculture, forestry, and hydropower exports.**
 
• Tourism is another significant contributor to Bhutan's economy, but it is regulated to preserve the country's cultural integrity.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Conservation:**
 
 
• Bhutan is renowned for its commitment to sustainability and environmental conservation.
 
• It is the only carbon-negative country in the world, meaning it absorbs more carbon dioxide than it emits.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Flag Symbolism:**

 
 
• The dragon depicted on Bhutan's flag holds jewels in its claws, representing national wealth and security.
 
• The yellow and orange colors of the flag symbolize the secular and spiritual traditions of Bhutan.
 
 
 
• **Gross National Happiness (GNH):**
 
 
• Bhutan follows the concept of **Gross National Happiness** instead of GDP to measure the country's progress and well-being.
 
• GNH emphasizes sustainable development, cultural preservation, environmental conservation, and good governance.
 
 
 
• **Tourism Policy:**
 
 
• Bhutan practices a "high-value, low-volume" tourism policy to ensure the preservation of its natural and cultural heritage.
 
• Visitors are required to pay a daily fee, which includes accommodation, meals, and guides.

questions.question: Which government scheme aims to provide financial support to senior citizens who may have lost their means of sustenance?

options.text: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)** is a component of the **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)**, launched by the Government of India.

• It was introduced in **1995** and revised in **2007** under the Ministry of Rural Development.

• The scheme provides a **monthly pension** to senior citizens aged **60 years and above** who belong to families living **below the poverty line (BPL)**.

• The amount of pension varies depending on the beneficiary's age:

• **60–79 years**: ₹200 per month from the central government (states can top up).

• **80 years and above**: ₹500 per month from the central government.

• IGNOAPS aims to provide **social security** and ensure the financial well-being of economically weaker sections of senior citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Atal Pension Yojana (APY):**

• Launched in **2015**, it is focused on providing a **guaranteed monthly pension** to workers in the **unorganized sector**.

• The entry age is **18–40 years**, and the pension amount ranges from ₹1,000 to ₹5,000, depending on contributions.

• It is co-contributory, with the government adding 50% of the contribution or ₹1,000 per year (whichever is lower) for eligible subscribers.

• **Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY):**

• Implemented by the **LIC of India**, this scheme aims to provide **pension security** to senior citizens aged **60 years and above**.

• It guarantees a fixed interest rate of **7.4% per annum** for 10 years, payable monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or yearly.

• The maximum purchase price under the scheme is ₹15 lakh.

• **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP):**

• Launched in **1995**, it is an umbrella scheme aimed at providing **social security** to the poor, including old age pension, widow pension, and disability pension.

• IGNOAPS is one of its key components, specifically targeted at senior citizens.

• **Key Differences:**

• **IGNOAPS:** Focuses on senior citizens in BPL families, providing small pensions.

• **APY:** Caters to unorganized workers, offering a range of pensions based on contributions.

• **PMVVY:** A fixed-income scheme for senior citizens with higher financial security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **IGNOAPS Implementation:**

• The scheme is implemented through **state governments and union territories**.

• Each state can add additional funds to the pension amount to enhance benefits.

• **Eligibility Verification:**

• BPL status is verified through the **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC)**.

• Beneficiaries need to provide proof of age and BPL status to avail of the benefits.

• **Challenges:**

• Low pension amounts under IGNOAPS remain a concern for ensuring adequate financial support.

• Coverage gaps and beneficiary identification issues persist in certain regions.

questions.question: Which Mughal Emperor is known for popularising pietra dura, or stone inlay technique, and the double dome in Indian architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Shah Jahan**, the fifth Mughal Emperor of India (reigned from **1628 to 1658**), is renowned for his patronage of architecture and his significant contributions to Indian art and culture.

• He is credited with popularizing the **pietra dura** technique, an intricate decorative art form where semi-precious stones are inlaid into marble or other stones to create floral designs, motifs, or images. This technique was extensively used in the construction of the **Taj Mahal**.

• Shah Jahan also introduced and perfected the concept of the **double dome** in Mughal architecture. The double dome not only added grandeur to structures but also improved their acoustics and provided better insulation.

• His architectural masterpieces include the **Taj Mahal** in Agra, the **Jama Masjid** in Delhi, and the **Red Fort** in Delhi, showcasing a blend of Persian, Indian, and Central Asian architectural styles.

• Shah Jahan's reign is often referred to as the **Golden Age of Mughal Architecture** due to the sheer magnificence and artistic advancement of the monuments built during his time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Pietra Dura Technique:**

• The term **pietra dura** originates from the Italian language, meaning "hard stone."

• It involves cutting and fitting stones like **lapis lazuli, onyx, jasper, and jade** into marble to create intricate patterns and designs.

• This technique was prominently used in the **Taj Mahal**, particularly on the cenotaphs and walls, adding to its elegance and artistic appeal.

• **Double Dome Architecture:**

• A double dome consists of two layers: an inner dome visible from the interior and an outer dome visible from the exterior.

• This innovation allowed for greater height and grandeur without making the interiors disproportionately large.

• Examples of double domes include the **Taj Mahal** and the **Humayun's Tomb** (the latter being a precursor to Shah Jahan's works).

• **Other Mughal Emperors:**

• **Babur:** The founder of the Mughal Empire, Babur focused more on military conquests than architecture, though he did establish Mughal garden traditions.

• **Akbar:** Known for his innovations in architecture, Akbar built the **Fatehpur Sikri** and promoted a blend of Indian and Persian styles, but he did not popularize pietra dura or double domes.

• **Aurangzeb:** The last major Mughal emperor, Aurangzeb's reign was marked by austerity, and he did not focus much on architectural advancements.

• **Significance of Shah Jahan's Contributions:**

• Shah Jahan's architectural marvels reflect the peak of Mughal art and aesthetics, blending Persian, Islamic, and Indian influences.

• His projects, especially the **Taj Mahal**, are globally recognized as symbols of love and artistic brilliance.

• The innovations like pietra dura and double domes had a lasting influence on Indian architecture and inspired future generations of artisans and builders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Taj Mahal:**

• Built between **1632 and 1653**, this mausoleum was constructed in memory of Shah Jahan's wife, **Mumtaz Mahal**.

• It is one of the **Seven Wonders of the World** and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• The Taj Mahal's pietra dura work and symmetrical design remain unparalleled in architectural history.

• **Jama Masjid:**

• Located in Old Delhi, the **Jama Masjid** was built between 1650 and 1656 and is one of the largest mosques in India.

• The mosque showcases Shah Jahan's preference for red sandstone and marble in architectural designs.

• **Red Fort:**

• The Red Fort, or **Lal Qila**, was constructed between 1638 and 1648 and served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors.

• It is an iconic symbol of Indian history and is where the Prime Minister hoists the national flag on **Independence Day** every year.

</ul

questions.question: What technological advancement is explicitly incorporated in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for faster justice delivery?

options.text: Use of drones for crime scene inspection

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electronic recording of witness testimony**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023** introduces modern technological advancements to streamline judicial processes and ensure faster delivery of justice.

• The incorporation of **electronic recording of witness testimony** is a critical feature aimed at reducing delays caused by manual procedures and ensuring accurate documentation of testimonies.

• **Electronic recording** minimizes the possibility of tampering, loss, or misinterpretation of witness statements, thereby enhancing the transparency and reliability of judicial proceedings.

• The use of technology ensures that the testimony remains accessible for future reference and provides a standardized method of recording across courts.

• This advancement aligns with the government’s vision to digitize and modernize the judicial infrastructure under initiatives like **Digital India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Importance of Witness Testimony:**

• Witness testimony serves as a crucial component of judicial trials, often being the deciding factor in criminal and civil cases.

• Ensuring the accuracy and security of witness statements is vital for maintaining the integrity of the judicial process.

• **Benefits of Electronic Recording:**

• Improves efficiency by eliminating manual transcription processes.

• Reduces the scope for human error during documentation.

• Enables secure storage and retrieval of recorded testimonies for future proceedings.

• **Global Practices:**

• Countries like the **United States** and **United Kingdom** have adopted electronic recording systems in courts to facilitate faster and more accurate documentation of proceedings.

• Such practices are considered benchmarks for judicial reforms worldwide.

• **Challenges in Implementation:**

• Initial infrastructure costs for setting up electronic recording systems in courts.

• Training judicial staff and ensuring their adaptability to new technologies.

• Addressing concerns related to data privacy and cybersecurity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023:**

• Aimed at reforming India’s judicial and law enforcement systems to make them more effective and citizen-centric.

• Emphasizes the use of technology to address long-pending issues such as delayed trials and outdated procedures.

• **Digital India Initiative:**

• Launched in **2015** by the Government of India, this initiative focuses on digitizing all aspects of governance.

• The judicial reforms under this initiative aim to modernize courtrooms and enhance public access to judicial services.

• **Other Technological Advancements:**

• Use of **video conferencing** for remote hearings, reducing the need for physical presence in courts.

• Development of **e-Courts** to digitize case filings and streamline judicial processes.

• Implementation of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** for legal research and case analysis.

3f

questions.question: Who among the following was the Chief Guest at India's Republic Day celebrations in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H.E. Prabowo Subianto**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **H.E. Prabowo Subianto**, the Defense Minister of **Indonesia**, was the Chief Guest at **India's Republic Day celebrations in 2025**.

• The tradition of inviting a foreign dignitary as the Chief Guest for Republic Day began in **1950**, with the Indonesian President Sukarno being the first Chief Guest.

• Indonesia shares **strong bilateral relations with India**, especially in areas such as defense, trade, culture, and strategic cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region.

• The visit of H.E. Prabowo Subianto as Chief Guest symbolizes the strengthening of ties between India and Indonesia, particularly in the context of **defense cooperation and maritime security**.

• The Republic Day parade is a significant event showcasing India's military strength, cultural heritage, and national achievements, providing an excellent platform to deepen diplomatic ties with the Chief Guest's country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **India-Indonesia Relations:**

• India and Indonesia are both members of key regional and global organizations such as **ASEAN, G20**, and **Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)**.

• They share a strong historical connection, particularly through the **spread of Hinduism and Buddhism** and cultural exchanges over centuries.

• Economic ties are significant, with bilateral trade valued at over **USD 20 billion** in recent years, focusing on commodities like crude oil, coal, and palm oil.

• Defense collaborations include joint naval exercises such as **Samudra Shakti** and cooperation in counterterrorism and regional security initiatives.

• **Significance of the Chief Guest at Republic Day:**

• The Chief Guest for Republic Day is typically a prominent leader or dignitary from a country with which India shares strategic, cultural, or economic ties.

• This tradition helps bolster bilateral relations and provides an opportunity to showcase India's military and cultural prowess to the international community.

• In recent years, notable Chief Guests have included **Barack Obama (2015)**, **Mohammed bin Salman (2019)**, and **Jair Bolsonaro (2020)**.

• **Republic Day Parade:**

• The parade is held annually on **January 26th** at Rajpath (now Kartavya Path) in New Delhi to commemorate the adoption of India's Constitution in **1950**.

• It showcases India's military might, cultural diversity, and achievements in science and technology.

• The parade includes tableaus representing various Indian states, cultural performances, and military displays such as missile systems and fighter jets.

• **H.E. Prabowo Subianto:**

• Prabowo Subianto is a prominent Indonesian politician and a retired army general, currently serving as Indonesia's **Defense Minister** since **2019**.

• He has been a key figure in enhancing Indonesia's defense capabilities and strengthening ties with global powers, including India.

• His visit to India as the Chief Guest highlights the strategic importance of **India-Indonesia defense cooperation** and the shared interest in maintaining stability in the Indo-Pacific region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Historical Background:**

• The first Republic Day parade in 1950 had **President Sukarno of Indonesia** as the Chief Guest, emphasizing the longstanding ties between the two nations.

• Indonesia, as the largest Muslim-majority country, holds a unique position in fostering interfaith dialogue and cultural exchange with India, a secular and diverse democracy.

• **Indo-Pacific Strategic Cooperation:**

• India and Indonesia play a crucial role in maintaining **maritime security** in the Indo-Pacific, a region critical for global trade and economic stability.

• Both countries are committed to upholding a **free, open, and inclusive Indo-Pacific**, ensuring the security of sea lanes and countering regional threats.

• **Defense Collaboration:**

• The two nations conduct joint military exercises, such as **Garuda Shakti** (army) and **Samudra Shakti** (navy), to enhance interoperability and mutual trust.

• India has also extended defense equipment and technical support to Indonesia, fostering a strong defense partnership.

</ul

questions.question: Talcher, a thermal power station in India, is in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Talcher** is a major industrial hub located in the Angul district of the state of **Odisha**, India.

• The **Talcher Thermal Power Station** is a significant coal-based power plant that contributes substantially to the power generation capacity of India.

• This power station is owned and operated by **NTPC Limited** (National Thermal Power Corporation Limited), one of India's largest energy conglomerates.

• Talcher is often referred to as the **"Coal City of Odisha"** due to its rich coal reserves and extensive mining activities. It is part of the Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) region.

• Odisha is one of the top coal-producing states in India, and Talcher plays a pivotal role in this sector by contributing significantly to the state's and the nation's energy requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Talcher's Industrial Significance:**

• Talcher hosts a variety of industries, including coal mining, power generation, and fertilizer production, making it an industrially rich region.

• The **Talcher Super Thermal Power Station**, also located in this region, has a power generation capacity of over 3,000 MW, making it one of the largest power plants in India.

• **Coal Mining in Talcher:**

• Talcher is part of the **Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL)**, a subsidiary of Coal India Limited (CIL), which is responsible for coal mining operations in the area.

• The coal mined here is primarily used for power generation and industrial purposes, catering to both domestic and industrial consumers across the country.

• **Location and Connectivity:**

• Talcher is well-connected by rail and road to major cities in Odisha and neighboring states, facilitating the transport of coal and other industrial goods.

• The nearest airport to Talcher is the **Biju Patnaik International Airport** in Bhubaneswar, located approximately 140 km away.

• **Power Generation in Odisha:**

• Odisha is a key contributor to India's energy sector, with several thermal, hydro, and renewable energy projects spread across the state.

• The state's energy production not only fulfills its own needs but also supplies electricity to other parts of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **NTPC Limited:**

• NTPC Limited, previously known as National Thermal Power Corporation, is a **central public sector undertaking** under the Ministry of Power, Government of India.

• It is India's largest power utility and contributes significantly to the country's electricity production.

• **Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL):**

• MCL is one of the major subsidiaries of **Coal India Limited (CIL)** and plays a crucial role in coal extraction in Odisha.

• The coalfields in and around Talcher are some of the most productive in the country.

• **Odisha's Energy Sector:**

• Odisha is among the leading states in India in terms of installed power generation capacity, with a mix of thermal, hydro, and renewable energy projects.

• The state's rich natural resources, including coal, bauxite, and iron ore, contribute to its industrial and energy production capabilities.

questions.question: In India, which of these geological formations hosts the most significant groundwater reservoirs for large-scale and extensive development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unconsolidated Formation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Unconsolidated formations** are loose, soft deposits made up of sand, silt, gravel, and clay, which are highly porous and permeable, making them the most significant geological formations for groundwater storage and extraction.

• These formations act as **aquifers**, which are underground layers of water-bearing permeable materials capable of storing and transmitting water in large quantities.

• In India, the major groundwater reservoirs are located in the **Indo-Gangetic Plain**, which is primarily composed of unconsolidated sediments deposited by rivers over millions of years.

• Owing to their high porosity and permeability, unconsolidated formations allow easy movement and storage of water, making them ideal for **large-scale groundwater development**, including irrigation, industrial use, and domestic water supply.

• Regions with unconsolidated formations, such as the Ganga-Brahmaputra basin and the coastal areas of India, are known to support extensive agricultural and urban water demands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Characteristics of Unconsolidated Formations:**

• These consist of loose sediments such as **sand, gravel, silt, and clay**, which are not cemented together.

• Due to their granular structure, they have high **porosity** (ability to store water) and high **permeability** (ease of water movement).

• Examples of areas with unconsolidated formations in India include the **Indo-Gangetic Plains** and the **deltaic regions** of rivers like the Ganga and Brahmaputra.

• **Importance of Groundwater Reservoirs:**

• Groundwater is a vital resource for **irrigation**, accounting for over 60% of agricultural water usage in India.

• It also provides drinking water to approximately **85% of rural households** and supports urban areas.

• Groundwater reservoirs in unconsolidated formations are particularly critical in regions with **seasonal rainfall**, such as India, where water storage is essential during dry periods.

• **Comparison with Other Formations:**

• **Semi-consolidated formations** have moderate porosity and permeability, making them less suitable for large-scale groundwater development.

• **Fissured and consolidated formations**, such as hard rock areas, have limited water storage capacity due to low porosity and rely on fractures and joints for water flow.

• Unconsolidated formations, by contrast, are more productive and reliable for meeting extensive groundwater needs.

• **Challenges in Groundwater Management:**

• Over-extraction of groundwater in unconsolidated formations can lead to issues like **aquifer depletion**, land subsidence, and water quality degradation.

• Effective management strategies, such as **artificial recharge** and sustainable water use practices, are crucial for preserving these vital resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Geological Formations in India:**

• **Unconsolidated formations:** Found mainly in alluvial regions like the **Indo-Gangetic Plains**. These are best suited for large-scale groundwater development.

• **Semi-consolidated formations:** Found in regions with sedimentary rocks like sandstones and limestones. Examples include parts of **central India**.

• **Fissured and consolidated formations:** Found in hard rock areas such as the **Deccan Plateau**, with limited groundwater storage potential.

• **Government Initiatives:**

• Programs like **Atal Bhujal Yojana** aim to ensure sustainable management of groundwater resources in India.

• Efforts to promote **rainwater harvesting** and artificial recharge are being implemented to replenish groundwater in unconsolidated formations.

``

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank:**

Magical realism blends magical or fantastical elements with realistic settings and events. The story narrates the rise and fall of the **Buendía family** in the fictional town of **Macondo**. This statement is **correct**.

• **Statement 2:** The novel does not present a linear historical account focused solely on Colombia's political events in the 20th century. Instead, it intertwines personal, familial, and mythical narratives with broader political and social commentary, often using non-linear storytelling. This statement is **incorrect**.

• The book is a **landmark work in Latin American literature**, widely celebrated for its depiction of history, culture, and politics through a blend of realism and fantasy.

• Gabriel Garcia Marquez won the **Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982**, largely due to the impact of *One Hundred Years of Solitude*, which is considered his magnum opus.

• Magical realism is a literary genre where magical elements are presented as a natural part of an otherwise realistic environment.

• In *One Hundred Years of Solitude*, events like ascensions to heaven, ghosts, and extraordinary weather phenomena are presented as everyday occurrences in Macondo.

• This style allows Marquez to explore the complexities of Latin American history and culture in a symbolic and imaginative manner.

• **Macondo:**

• Macondo is a fictional town that serves as the primary setting for the novel.

• It is inspired by Marquez's hometown of **Aracataca, Colombia**.

• The town becomes a microcosm of Latin American society, reflecting its struggles with colonialism, political turmoil, and modernization.

• **The Buendía Family:**

• The narrative spans seven generations of the Buendía family, chronicling their triumphs, tragedies, and eventual decline.

• The family members often repeat the same mistakes, symbolizing the cyclical nature of history and human behavior.

• **Political and Social Commentary:**

• While the novel is not a direct historical account, it draws heavily on the political and social history of Colombia and Latin America.

• Events such as civil wars, the banana massacre, and the exploitation of workers by foreign companies are allegorically depicted in the story.

• **Significance of the Novel:**

• *One Hundred Years of Solitude* is considered one of the greatest literary works of the 20th century.

• It played a crucial role in the rise of the **Latin American Boom**, a literary movement that brought global attention to Latin American authors.

• The novel has been translated into more than 40 languages and has sold over 50 million copies worldwide.

Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the borrowing powers of States in India?

1) A State requires the Centre's consent for internal borrowing if it owes any debt to the Centre.

2) No State can raise loans from foreign sources without prior approval of the Union Government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Statement 1 and 2 are Correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Statement 1:** A State requires the Centre's consent for internal borrowing if it owes any debt to the Centre.

- This is correct as per **Article 293(3)** of the **Constitution of India**. A State that owes loans to the Centre must seek prior approval before borrowing further.

• **Statement 2:** No State can raise loans from foreign sources without prior approval of the Union Government.

- This is correct as the borrowing of funds from foreign sources by States is regulated by the **Union Government** to ensure compliance with international agreements and the country’s financial stability.

• The borrowing powers of States are governed by **Article 293** of the Constitution, which imposes restrictions to prevent financial instability or unsanctioned debts.

• The Union Government oversees borrowing activities of States to maintain fiscal discipline and ensure coordination between States and the Centre.

• Thus, both statements are correct, and the correct answer is **3) Statement 1 and 2 are Correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__

• **Article 293 of the Constitution:** 

• **Clause (1):** A State can borrow within the territory of India upon the security of its Consolidated Fund.

• **Clause (3):** If a State owes any loans to the Union Government, it must seek prior approval for further borrowing.

• **Clause (4):** The Union Government can impose conditions on borrowing to ensure compliance with financial stability norms.

• **Foreign Borrowing:** 

• States cannot independently negotiate loans with foreign entities without Union Government approval.

• This ensures that external borrowings align with national interests and international agreements.

• **Fiscal Federalism in India:** 

• The financial relationship between the Centre and States is governed by Constitutional provisions to maintain fiscal discipline.

• The **Finance Commission** periodically reviews the allocation of resources and borrowing limits.

• **Borrowing Limits:** 

• The Union Government sets borrowing limits for States based on economic conditions and fiscal parameters.

• This is done to prevent excessive debt accumulation and ensure financial sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Union Control Over Borrowing:** The Union Government ensures that borrowing by States does not conflict with national financial policies and international obligations.

• **Finance Commission:** The Finance Commission recommends measures to manage State borrowing and allocates funds to ensure equitable distribution.

• **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act:** This Act promotes financial discipline by prescribing fiscal targets for both the Centre and States.

Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): GDP doesn't really tell the whole story when it comes to how well people in a country are actually doing.

Reason (R): That's mainly because it doesn't take into account stuff like wear and tear of machines, pollution, or even how the money is divided among people.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Assertion (A): GDP doesn't really tell the whole story when it comes to how well people in a country are actually doing.** 
• Gross Domestic Product (**GDP**) measures the total economic output of a country but does not reflect the overall well-being of citizens. 
• It does not account for factors such as income inequality, environmental degradation, or the quality of life. ***Hence, the assertion is correct.*** 
• **Reason (R): That's mainly because it doesn't take into account stuff like wear and tear of machines, pollution, or even how the money is divided among people.** 
• **GDP** primarily measures economic activity and ignores externalities like **pollution**, **resource depletion**, or **income distribution.** 
• It also excludes factors such as the depreciation of capital goods (wear and tear of machines) and how wealth is distributed among individuals. ***Hence, the reason is correct.*** 
• The reason directly explains why GDP fails to fully capture the well-being of citizens. ***Thus, it is the correct explanation of the assertion.*** 
• ***Therefore, both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Limitations of GDP as an Indicator:** 
• **Environmental Costs:** GDP does not consider the negative effects of economic activities, such as **pollution** or depletion of natural resources. 
• **Income Inequality:** GDP measures total output but does not show how income is distributed across the population. High GDP can coexist with **widespread poverty**. 
• **Non-Market Activities:** Informal sector activities, household labor, and volunteer work are excluded from GDP calculations, despite their contribution to society. 
• **Depreciation:** GDP does not account for the wear and tear of capital goods (known as **depreciation**), which can affect future productivity. 
• **Quality of Life:** GDP focuses on quantity rather than quality. Factors like **healthcare**, **education**, or **happiness** are not directly measured. 
• **Alternative Measures of Well-Being:** 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):** Combines measures of **health**, **education**, and **income** to provide a broader perspective on well-being. 
• **Gross National Happiness (GNH):** Used by countries like Bhutan to prioritize **happiness** and quality of life over economic output. 
• **Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI):** Adjusts GDP by considering factors such as **environmental costs**, **social costs**, and income inequality. 
• **Green GDP:** Accounts for environmental degradation and resource depletion alongside economic growth. 
• **Important Points:** 
• Economists and policymakers often use GDP as a benchmark but recognize the need for supplementary indicators to assess a country’s overall progress. 
• In recent years, global organizations like the **United Nations** and **World Bank** have emphasized the importance of inclusive growth and sustainable development. 
• Countries are increasingly adopting multidimensional indices to address the limitations of GDP and focus on long-term well-being.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements on the Green Hydrogen Mission:

1. It aims to make India a global hub for production and export of green hydrogen.

2. The mission targets production of 10 MMT by 2030.

3. Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using renewable energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Statement 1: It aims to make India a global hub for production and export of green hydrogen.** 

• This statement is correct. The **National Green Hydrogen Mission** was introduced to position India as a key player in the global green hydrogen market, encouraging both domestic production and export opportunities.

• The initiative aligns with India’s commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and achieving **net-zero carbon emissions by 2070**.

• **Statement 2: The mission targets production of 10 MMT by 2030.**

• This statement is incorrect. While the mission has ambitious production targets, the actual target for green hydrogen production by 2030 is **5 MMT (Million Metric Tonnes)** as per the official framework of the National Green Hydrogen Mission.

• The focus is to enhance domestic production and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.

• **Statement 3: Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using renewable energy.**

• This statement is correct. Green hydrogen is generated through the process of **electrolysis**, where water is split into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity sourced from **renewable energy** like solar or wind power.

• This makes green hydrogen a sustainable and clean alternative to conventional hydrogen production methods, which rely on fossil fuels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **National Green Hydrogen Mission:**

• Launched by the **Government of India** in **2022**, the mission aims to make India a leader in the production and use of green hydrogen.

• The mission will help in reducing India’s dependency on imported energy and contribute significantly to its energy transition efforts.

• It is expected to attract investments worth **Rs. 8 lakh crore** and create over **6 lakh jobs**.

• The mission is part of India’s strategy to meet its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the Paris Agreement.

• **Green Hydrogen:**

• It is hydrogen produced through **electrolysis** using electricity generated from renewable energy sources.

• This hydrogen has a variety of applications, including in industries like steel, cement, and chemicals, as well as in transportation and energy storage.

• It is considered a key fuel for the future due to its potential to decarbonize sectors that are difficult to electrify directly.

• **Key Environmental Benefits:**

• Green hydrogen reduces carbon emissions significantly compared to grey hydrogen, which is derived from natural gas.

• It supports the global transition to **clean energy** and helps combat climate change.

• **Current Global Scenario:**

• Countries like Germany, Japan, and Australia are investing heavily in green hydrogen technologies.

• India’s mission places it among the leading nations aiming to scale up green hydrogen production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Green Hydrogen Production Technologies:**

• **Electrolysis:** The most common method for producing green hydrogen using water and renewable electricity.

• **Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting:** Uses sunlight to split water into hydrogen and oxygen.

• Research is ongoing to improve the efficiency of these technologies and reduce production costs.

• **Challenges in Green Hydrogen Adoption:**

• The high cost of production and lack of infrastructure for storage and distribution are key barriers.

• Scaling up requires significant investments and technological advancements.

• **Future Prospects:**

• With global emphasis on achieving net-zero emissions, green hydrogen is expected to play a pivotal role in transforming the energy landscape.

• India’s proactive initiatives under the Green Hydrogen Mission aim to position the country as a major player in this emerging sector.

questions.question: The term 'Navratnas' in public sector reform refers to:

options.text: Public enterprises granted autonomy for better performance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public enterprises granted autonomy for better performance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The term **‘Navratnas’** refers to select public sector enterprises in India that have been granted autonomy to improve their operational performance.

• This autonomy allows these enterprises to operate independently without significant interference from the government in decision-making processes, enabling them to compete in the global market.

• Navratnas are part of a larger classification system within India’s public sector units (PSUs), which includes **Maharatnas**, **Navratnas**, and **Miniratnas**, based on their financial performance and operational capabilities.

• The status of Navratna is granted to PSUs that meet certain financial criteria, such as earning a net profit, maintaining a good net worth, and achieving specific annual turnover thresholds.

• Navratna PSUs are empowered to make strategic investments, form joint ventures, and undertake mergers and acquisitions without requiring prior approval from the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Criteria for Navratna Status:**

• PSUs must achieve a score of 60 out of 100 in six performance parameters: net profit, net worth, total manpower cost, productivity of capital and assets, and earnings per share.

• They must also maintain a minimum annual turnover of Rs. 2,000 crore and a net profit of Rs. 30 crore.

• **Features of Navratna Companies:**

• Navratna PSUs can invest up to Rs. 1,000 crore or 15% of their net worth in a single project without government approval.

• They are allowed to enter into joint ventures and form alliances with foreign companies to enhance their operational efficiency.

• **Examples of Navratna PSUs:**

• Companies such as Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), and National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO) have been granted Navratna status.

• These companies operate in diverse sectors, including defense, aerospace, energy, and minerals.

• **Difference Between Navratna and Maharatna:**

• Maharatna companies have even greater autonomy than Navratna companies. For instance, Maharatnas can invest up to Rs. 5,000 crore in a single project without government approval.

• Navratna status is often a stepping stone for PSUs to achieve Maharatna status based on their sustained financial and operational performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Historical Context:**

• The Navratna status was introduced in **1997** as part of India’s economic reforms to enhance the efficiency of PSUs.

• This initiative was aimed at encouraging PSUs to operate more competitively and contribute to national economic growth.

• **Impact of Autonomy:**

• Navratna PSUs have played a crucial role in driving industrial growth, creating employment opportunities, and earning significant foreign exchange for India.

• They are often considered benchmarks for operational excellence within the public sector.

• **Global Competitiveness:**

• By granting autonomy, Navratna companies have been able to expand their operations internationally, competing with private and multinational corporations.

• For example, ONGC Videsh Ltd., a subsidiary of ONGC (a Navratna company), has successfully acquired oil and gas assets abroad.
